prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable solution gives 8,000,000,000 people a free health check every year; the WHO-World Bank UHC Global Monitoring Report 2025 finds 4.6 billion people still lack essential health services (https://www.news-medical.net/news/20251206/Billions-still-lack-essential-health-services-despite-worldwide-gains-in-coverage.aspx). The largest national free check programmes are partial: Indonesia's Cek Kesehatan Gratis (launched February 2025) reached about a quarter of its population in its first year (https://en.antaranews.com/news/403778/free-health-check-program-covers-25-pct-population-in-its-first-year), Vietnam about 30% by July 2026 (https://dtinews.dantri.com.vn/print/20260724161740947.htm), China's free check covers only residents aged 65 and over, and England's NHS Health Check (ages 40-74) had 35% uptake of invitations in 2025/26 (https://www.covermagazine.co.uk/news/4532410/uptake-nhs-health-checks-hits-lowest-level-decade). Honest limit: national free-check models are proven and published; the unsolved part is low-cost, high-uptake delivery at global scale, and a task that only restates a national programme design is not new work.
